<Conflict due to outdated information> — d8 contains outdated pre‑2023 information, while all other relevant sources confirm the euro adoption in January 2023.

The conflict arises because d8, dated December 2022, speaks of Croatia's planned adoption of the euro on Jan. 1, 2023 as a future event, whereas d1–d7 and d9 state the euro is the current currency, having been adopted on that date. This is a clear case of outdated information versus current fact.

The evidence from d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d7, and d9 consistently states that Croatia adopted the euro as its official currency on 1 January 2023, making it the current national currency. The outdated snippet in d8 does not contradict this fact; it merely reflects the pre‑adoption perspective.

Croatia's current national currency is the euro. Croatia adopted the euro as its official currency on 1 January 2023, replacing the Croatian kuna [d1][d2][d4]. The euro is now the sole legal tender, as confirmed by official sources including the European Commission and the European Central Bank [d3][d7][d9].
